title.narrative: Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Southeast Asia Regional Economic Corridor and Connectivity Project for Laos is to improve regional and domestic trade and climate resilient transport connectivity along an East-West corridor in Southeast Asia, and to provide immediate and effective response in case of an eligible crisis or emergency. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Lao PDR and Regional connectivity enhancement, has the following sub-components: (i) National Road No. 2 West (NR2W) climate resilient improvement and maintenance; (ii) Local Road climate resilient improvement and maintenance; (iii) Improvement of the border crossing facilities; and (iv) Implementation and supervision support. 2) The second component, Logistics services development and border-crossing management, has the following sub-components: (i) Logistics facilities development; (ii) Regional integration and cross-border transport agreements; and (iii) Strengthening capacity of Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) and Border Management. 3) The third component, Strengthening institutional capacity and regulatory framework in agriculture, transport, and investments planning, has the following sub-components: (i) Support on agricultural trade and SPS Management; and (ii) Institutional capacity development for transport sector. 4) The fourth component, Project Management, will provide technical and operational assistance for strengthening the environmental and social (E&S) capacity of agencies concerned at national and local levels, the day-to-day management, and monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of the project; digitized tools to support business processes and M&E; and the carrying out of technical and financial audits.

To improve regional and domestic trade and climate resilient transport connectivity along an East-West corridor in Southeast Asia, and to provide immediate and effective response in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

condition.narrative: Annual Work Plans and BudgetSection I.D of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient shall furnish to the Association,not later than December 15 of each Fiscal Year during the implementation of the Project (or such other date as the Association mayagree) for the Association's no-objection, an Annual Work Plan and Budget (“AWPB”) containing all Project activities and EligibleExpenditures proposed to be included in the Project in the Recipient's following Fiscal Year.

Contingent Emergency Response Component (“CERC”)Section I.H of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement1. In order to ensure theproper implementation of contingent emergency response activities under Part 5 of the Project (“Contingent Emergency ResponsePart”), the Recipient shall ensure that:(a) the CERC Manual is prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to theAssociation, which shall set forth detailed implementation arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part, including: (i)any structures or institutional arrangements for coordinating and implementing the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (ii)specific activities which may be included in the Contingent Emergency Response Part, Eligible Expenditures required therefor(“Emergency Expenditures”), and any procedures for such inclusion; (iii) financial management arrangements for the ContingentEmergency Response Part; (iv) procurement methods and procedures for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; (v) documentationrequired for withdrawals of Financing amounts to finance Emergency Expenditures; (vi) a description of the environmental and socialassessment and management arrangements for the Contingent Emergency Response Part; and (vii) a template Emergency ActionPlan;(b) the Emergency Action Plan is prepared and adopted in form and substance acceptable to the Association;the EmergencyResponse Part is carried out in accordance with the CERC Manual and the Emergency Action Plan; provided, however, that in the eventof any inconsistency between the provisions of the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan and this Agreement, the provisions ofthis Agreement shall prevail; and(d) neither the CERC Manual or the Emergency Action Plan is amended, suspended, abrogated,repealed or waived without the prior written approval by the Association.2. The Recipient shall ensure that the structures andarrangements referred to in the CERC Manual are maintained throughout the implementation of the Contingent Emergency Response Part,with adequate staff and resources satisfactory to Association.3. The Recipient shall ensure that:(a) the environmental andsocial instruments required for the Contingent Emergency Response Part are prepared, disclosed and adopted in accordance with theCERC Manual and the ESCP, and in form and substance acceptable to the Association; and(b) the Contingent Emergency Response Partis carried out in accordance with the environmental and social instruments in a manner acceptable to the Association.4. Theactivities under the Contingency Emergency Response Part shall be undertaken only after an Eligible Crisis or Emergency hasoccurred.

Environmental and Social StandardsSections I.G. of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient shall ensure that theProject is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in a manner acceptable to the Association.Without limitation upon paragraph 1 above, the Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with theEnvironmental and Social Commitment Plan, including Environmental and Social Instruments referred to therein (ESCP), in a manneracceptable to the Association. To this end, the Recipient shall ensure that: (a) the measures and actions specified in the ESCP areimplemented with due diligence and efficiency, and as further specified in the ESCP and the Safeguards Instruments; (b) sufficientfunds are available to cover the costs of implementing the ESCP; (c) policies, procedures and qualified staff are maintained toenable it to implement the ESCP, as further specified in the ESCP; and (d) the ESCP, or any provision thereof, is not amended,repealed, suspended or waived, except as the Association shall otherwise agree in writing, as specified in the ESCP, and ensurethat the revised ESCP is disclosed promptly thereafter.

Institutional ArrangementsSection I.A of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement1. Project Steering CommitteeThe Recipientshall maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, a multi-sectorial Project Steering Committee, with a mandate,composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for, inter alia: overseeing the overallProject implementation and addressing policy and implementation issues. 2. Project Coordination CommitteeThe Recipient shallmaintain, throughout the Project implementation period, a Project Coordination Committee, with a mandate, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for, inter alia: overall Project coordination including managing,facilitating and coordinating the Project implementation and serving as a secretary to the Project Steering Committee. 3. Project Management UnitThe Recipient shall maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, the Project Management Unit,with a mandate, staffing and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be responsible for, inter alia: (a) the overallmanagement of the Project, including the preparation of Annual Work Plans and Budgets; (b) the overall administration of financialmanagement, procurement, environmental and social risk management; (c) overall monitoring, evaluation and reporting of Projectactivities; and (d) reporting to the Project Steering Committee on the implementation of Project activities.4. MPWT ProjectImplementation Structures The Recipient shall maintain, throughout the Project implementation period, Project implementationstructures within MPWT to support the PMU in implementing the Project.

OPBRC Sustainability PlanSection I.F of Schedule 2 to the Financing AgreementThe Recipient shall adopt, not later than 12 monthsprior to the Closing Date, a sustainability plan, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association, specifying actions andbudget designed to ensure the continued and effective implementation of the OPBRC in the period after the Closing Date, including,inter alia, financial, institutional sustainability, and monitoring and supervision measures to be put in place by MPWT for thefull period of the operation and maintenance phase of the OPBRC.

Specific Institutional and Implementation Arrangements for Part 2.1 of the Project.Section I.B of Schedule 2 to the FinancingAgreement1. In order to facilitate the carrying out of Part 2.1 of the Project, the Recipient shall take all necessary steps toput in place and maintain legal, financial and institutional arrangements, acceptable to the Association and in accordance withfurther details set forth in the Project Implementation Manual, for the implementation of activities under Part 2.1 of the Projectthrough public-private partnership arrangements.2. Without limitation to the generality of the provisions of Section I.B.1above, the Recipient through MPWT:(a) by not later than thirty (30) months after the Effective Date (or such other date as theAssociation has confirmed in writing to the Recipient as reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances, as determined by theAssociation), select and engage the services of one or more transaction advisors, each with qualifications and experience and underterms of reference acceptable to the Association, to provide advisory services necessary for the design and execution of thepublic-private partnership arrangements;(b) by not later than thirty (30) months after the Effective Date (or such other date asthe Association has confirmed in writing to the Recipient as reasonable and acceptable under the circumstances, as determined bythe Association), complete the establishment and/or designation of an entity, with a mandate, composition and resourcessatisfactory to the Association (“Contracting Entity”), for purposes of, inter alia, contracting with one or more private sectorentities in accordance with the provisions of Section I.B.2(c) below; and (c) by not later than thirty (30) months after thetransaction advisory contract(s) commence (or such other date as the Association has confirmed in writing the Recipient asreasonable and acceptable under the circumstances, as determined by the Association), cause the Contracting Entity to enter intolegally binding contractual arrangements with one or more private sector entities, each in form and substance satisfactory to theAssociating, to carry out the public-private partnership arrangements under Part 2.1 of the Project (PPP Contract(s).3. TheRecipient shall cause: (a) the Contracting Entity to exercise its rights and carry out its obligations under the PPP Contract(s) soas to protect the interests of the Recipient and the Association and to accomplish the purposes of Part 2.1 of the Project. Exceptas the Association shall otherwise agree in writing, the Recent shall ensure that the Contracting Entity shall not assign, amend,abrogate or waive the respective the PPP Contract(s), or any provisions thereof, or permit any entity or agency to do so

Technical AuditsSection I.E of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement1. The Recipient shall, not later than September 15, 2023,appoint and thereafter maintain throughout the Project implementation period, an independent technical auditor, with terms ofreference and qualifications satisfactory to the Association, for the purpose of carrying out independent technical audits of theworks financed under the Project.2. Without limitation on its other reporting obligations under this Agreement, the Recipientshall: (a) not later than April 30 of each year during the implementation of the Project, commencing on April 30, 2024, furnish tothe Association the reports of the independent technical auditor referred to in paragraph 1 above; and (b) promptly thereafter takemeasures, acceptable to the Association, to address the findings and implement the recommendations of each such report.

title.narrative: Time taken to obtain SPS certification for agriculture trade

comment.narrative:
Measure the total time required for Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) clearance of selected plants and plant products, animals and animal products, and food products intended for export. This measure encompasses the following components: (i) Border Clearance Time: The period needed for document review to confirm completeness and compliance with SPS requirements. (ii) Inspection: The time taken by SPS staff to inspect plants and plant products, animals and animal products, and food products at the border checkpoint. (iii) Customs Clearance: The duration required for customs staff to verify documents, conduct inspections (if necessary), and release the goods.
On track. On track. Reduced from average 10.80 days in 2022 to 8.65 days in Sept 2025 - DOA Time reduced from 9.04 days to 6.57 Days - DLF time increase from 11.74 days to 12.44 days (due to additional steps) - FDD time reduced from 11.61 days to 6.93 days

title.narrative: Reduction in time taken for processing permits in agricultural trade

comment.narrative:
Measure the reduction in time required to process permits (SPS-related certificates) for Plants and Plant Products, Animal and Animal Products, and Food Products export, expressed as a percentage reduction in time compared to the baseline time. It covers SPS certificates for the export of Plants and Plant Products, Animal and Animal Products, and Food Products. The scope includes pre-border processing time, starting from the submission of required documentation by traders for SPS certificates, document inspection, testing of samples etc. and finally the issuance of the SPS certificates by the concerned authorities for Plants and Plant Products, Animal and Animal Products, and Food Products.
On track. Reduced time from 46.5 days in year 2022 to 35.17 days (24.4% reduction in time) - Plants and Plant Products: Reduced 33.9% - Animal and Animal Products: Reduced 1.1% - Food Products: Reduced 37.4%%
